blockingFindings.title: R1 import-path migration is not directly covered
blockingFindings.issue: R1 requires import paths to be adjusted to the new src/ structure, but the R1 test only checks that relocated files exist. Later tests exercise only workflow --help and a few content sweeps, so production files could still contain stale imports such as experimental/workflow or wrong relative paths in commands that are not loaded by help.
blockingFindings.requiredChange: Add a spec-local assertion that src/workflow/**/*.js contains no imports/requires from experimental/ and either imports all relocated modules or exercises representative command module loading through the new src/workflow paths.
blockingFindings.whyBlocking: The acceptance requirement explicitly includes import-path adjustment, and the current tests can pass file-existence checks without verifying that relocated production modules are wired to the new location.

advisoryFindings.title: R8 notice wording is stricter than the requirement wording
advisoryFindings.improvement: Consider allowing a Japanese equivalent or a semantically equivalent phrase for "usage patterns may change" if the documentation may be localized.
advisoryFindings.whyNonBlocking: The current literal phrase is acceptable if the intended documentation wording is fixed in English, but it may make a should-level documentation requirement unnecessarily brittle.

advisoryFindings.title: R9 graduation-criteria assertions are broad
advisoryFindings.improvement: Consider checking for all four required concepts with slightly more specific terms, especially ideas-to-publish flow and fixed status enum contract.
advisoryFindings.whyNonBlocking: The test does cover the broad documentation requirement, but a vague mention of publish or status enum could satisfy it without clearly documenting the intended graduation criteria.
